label: F-01
title: simulate-yield.sh still feeds MockAutoDOLA after story 089's repoint, so dev's yield-simulation step reaches no live DOLA consumer (disclosed, unlanded story-089 follow-up)
fingerprintVerified: re-derived by finding-manager as sha256(contract:function:rootCauseClass:entryPoint); matches verbatim
description: dev's step 6 ('Simulating yield') mints 2,300 DOLA into the vault at progress.31337.json .contracts.MockAutoDOLA. Since story 089's Phase 9.7, the minter, StableStakerV2 and SYA all sit on YieldStrategyDola over MockSDOLA. SYA no longer lists the legacy strategy, and its withdrawer flag there is revoked. The simulated yield therefore lands only in the legacy vault, and nothing in the live system can skim it. Story 089 (Implementation Notes, line 104; Review, line 216) records this as an out-of-file-list follow-up. simulate-yield.sh is unchanged since baseline, so the follow-up has not landed.
impact: UI developers running npm run dev get no simulated DOLA surplus on the live strategy; SYA claim / yield displays are unaffected by the step that claims to drive them. Local only; no mainnet effect.
evidence: Executed: MockAutoDOLA totalAssets 1000.12 -> 3300.12 DOLA; SYA isRegisteredStrategy(legacy) = false, (sDOLA) = true; legacy totalBalanceOf(minter) = 3,299.64 DOLA, unreachable (see DEV39-02). Story 089 lines 104, 182, 216, 261.
attackPath: 1. Story 089 Phase 9.7 repoints the minter, StableStakerV2 and SYA to YieldStrategyDola over MockSDOLA, and revokes SYA's withdrawer flag on the legacy strategy.
2. simulate-yield.sh (unchanged since baseline) still mints into .contracts.MockAutoDOLA.
3. The yield lands on a de-registered strategy, so the SYA claim and yield displays are not driven by the step that is meant to drive them.

justification: Routed to spec-conformance as F-01 at QA severity, not as a Low defect. Story 089 itself scoped the retargeting out and recorded it as a disclosed follow-up ([low], carried at auto-complete), so 089's own stated behaviour is not violated. What is broken is a consequence: the earlier dev behaviour (step 6 simulates yield for the live system) silently stopped working when 089 landed, and the follow-up has not been landed or ticketed as its own story. Law 2 says to surface that to the owner and not bury it in the QA bundle. Because the story disclosed it, this is an outstanding-work note rather than a hidden defect. There is no security or value impact, so no Low/Medium rating. The UI-mock ruling does not apply, because this concerns dev's internal coherence, not mainnet fidelity.
recommendation: Land the story-089 follow-up. Retarget simulate-yield.sh to .contracts.MockSDOLA (or call MockSDOLA.addYield), and assert that YieldStrategyDola's surplus for SYA increased after the step. If the work stays deferred, open a tracked story for it so the disclosure does not live only in 089's review notes.
